verses.text: The war between Saul's family and David's family went on for a long time. David grew stronger and stronger, while Saul's family grew weaker and weaker.
Sons were born to David in Hebron. His firstborn was Amnon, whose mother was Ahinoam from Jezreel.
His second son was Chileab, whose mother was Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel. The third was Absalom, the son of Maacah, the daughter of Talmai king of Geshur.
The fourth was Adonijah, the son of Haggith. The fifth was Shephatiah, the son of Abital.
The sixth was Ithream, whose mother was Eglah, David's wife. These sons were born to David in Hebron.
While the war went on between Saul's family and David's family, Abner was making himself more and more powerful in Saul's family.
Saul had a slave wife named Rizpah, the daughter of Aiah. Ishbosheth said to Abner, "Why did you sleep with my father's slave wife?"

Abner was very angry at what Ishbosheth said. He answered, "Do you think I am a dog working for Judah? Until today I have been loyal to the family of your father Saul, to his brothers, and to his friends. I have not handed you over to David. Yet today you accuse me of doing wrong with this woman!
May God punish me, and even more, if I do not do for David what the LORD promised him with an oath:
to take the kingdom away from Saul's family and to set up David's throne over Israel and Judah, from Dan all the way to Beersheba."
Ishbosheth could not say another word to Abner, because he was afraid of him.
Then Abner sent messengers to David to speak for him. They said, "Who does this land belong to? Make an agreement with me, and I will help you bring all Israel over to your side."
David said, "Good. I will make an agreement with you. But I ask one thing of you: Do not come to see me unless you first bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come."
Then David sent messengers to Ishbosheth, Saul's son, to say, "Give me my wife Michal. I paid for her with one hundred foreskins of the Philistines."
So Ishbosheth sent men to take her away from her husband, Paltiel son of Laish.
Her husband went with her, crying all the way, and followed her as far as Bahurim. Then Abner said to him, "Go back home!" So he went back.
Abner spoke with the leaders of Israel. He said, "For some time now you have wanted David to be your king.
Now do it! For the LORD has said about David, 'Through my servant David I will save my people Israel from the Philistines and from all their enemies.'"
Abner also spoke to the people of Benjamin. Then he went to Hebron to tell David everything that Israel and the whole tribe of Benjamin had agreed to.
Abner came to David at Hebron with twenty men, and David made a feast for Abner and the men with him.

Abner said to David, "Let me go now and gather all Israel to you, my lord the king. They will make an agreement with you, and you will rule over everything you want." So David sent Abner away, and he left in peace.

Just then David's servants and Joab came back from a raid, bringing a large amount of goods they had taken. But Abner was no longer with David in Hebron, because David had sent him away, and he had left in peace.
When Joab and all his army arrived, Joab was told, "Abner son of Ner came to the king, and the king let him go, and he has left in peace."
So Joab went to the king and said, "What have you done? Abner came to you. Why did you let him go? Now he is gone!
You know Abner son of Ner. He came to trick you, to learn all your movements, coming and going, and to find out everything you are doing."
Then Joab left David and sent messengers after Abner. They brought him back from the well of Sirah, but David did not know about it.

When Abner came back to Hebron, Joab took him aside in the gateway as if to talk with him privately. There he stabbed him in the stomach, and Abner died. Joab did this to pay him back for the death of his brother Asahel.
Later, when David heard about it, he said, "I and my kingdom are forever innocent before the LORD of the death of Abner son of Ner.

Let the blame fall on Joab and on all his father's family. May Joab's family always have someone with a running sore, or a skin disease, or someone who needs a walking stick, or who dies by the sword, or who does not have enough food."
So Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner, because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.

Then David said to Joab and all the people with him, "Tear your clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourn as you walk in front of Abner's body." King David himself walked behind the stretcher carrying the body.
They buried Abner in Hebron. The king cried loudly at Abner's grave, and all the people cried too.
The king sang this sad song for Abner: "Should Abner have died like a fool dies?
Your hands were not tied, and your feet were not put in chains. You fell like someone who falls before wicked men." And all the people cried over him again.

Then all the people came to urge David to eat something while it was still day. But David made a promise: "May God punish me, and even more, if I taste bread or anything else before the sun goes down."
All the people noticed this, and it pleased them. In fact, everything the king did pleased all the people.
So that day all the people and all Israel understood that the king had no part in the killing of Abner son of Ner.
Then the king said to his servants, "Don't you know that a great leader has fallen in Israel today?
Even though I am the chosen king, I am weak today. These sons of Zeruiah are too hard for me. May the LORD pay back the evildoer for the evil he has done."
